title: Time-Dynamic AI Models to Predict Quality of Life in Patients With Breast Cancer: Development and Validation Study Using the EORTC BALANCE Cohort.
summary: Time-dynamic ML models used earlier EORTC quality-of-life assessments and clinical data to predict later impairment in 6,316 patients across more than 70,000 assessment pairs. Independent NKI validation AUCs ranged 0.643–0.837, with substantial overconfidence and weaker calibration for some outcomes.
ai_technology: Gradient boosting and other classifiers used prior QLQ-C30 assessments, clinical data and time since assessment to predict later quality-of-life impairment.
organization: Health Outcomes Research Unit, University Hospital of Psychiatry II, Medical University of Innsbruck, Austria; Department of Psychosocial Research and Epidemiology, The Netherlands Cancer Institute, Amsterdam, The Netherlands; Evaluation Software Development GmbH, Austria; Department of Medical and Clinical Psychology, Tilburg University, The Netherlands; Netherlands Comprehensive Cancer Organisation (IKNL), Utrecht, The Netherlands; Division of Imaging and Oncology, University Medical Centre Utrecht, The Netherlands; Cancer Survivorship Outcomes and Epidemiology, German Cancer Research Center, Germany; EORTC Quality of Life Group

evidence.tested: Across 6,316 patients and more than 70,000 assessment pairs, independent NKI validation AUC ranged from 0.643 to 0.837; the paper also reports substantial overconfidence and calibration weaknesses for low-prevalence symptoms.
evidence.unknown: Five cohorts were used for development and an independent NKI cohort for external validation. Calibration slopes were 0.089–0.286; the primary preprint posted 2025-08-18 reports the same core result as the 2026 journal version.
evidence.ai_role: The models predicted later patient-reported quality-of-life impairment with independent-cohort discrimination, while calibration limits remained substantial.

source_review.scope: JMIR v1 primary preprint and final full text compared for result-bearing version; Methods, Results, independent validation and calibration checked.
